record.original_question: Let r >= 2 and N >= 1 be integers, with N allowed to be sufficiently large as a function of r. Suppose r(N+1) points P_{ij} in R^N are indexed by 1 <= i <= r and 1 <= j <= N+1, and suppose 0 belongs to conv{P_{1j},...,P_{rj}} for every j. Suppose further that {1,2,...,N+1} is partitioned into color classes C_1,...,C_m with |C_k| <= r-1 for every k. Must there exist choices k_1,...,k_{N+1} in {1,...,r} such that 0 belongs to conv{P_{k_1,1},...,P_{k_{N+1},N+1}} and, whenever a and b are distinct indices in the same color class C_k, the selected labels satisfy k_a != k_b?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. (A Multicolored Caratheodory Conjecture). Let r >= 2 and N >= 1 be integers. Suppose we are given r(N+1) points Pij in RN that are indexed by 1 <= i <= r and 1 <= j <= N+1. Assume that 0 is in conv{P1j,...,Prj} for all 1 <= j <= N+1. Assume further that the index set {1,2,...,N+1} is partitioned as C1 union ... union Cm such that all color classes are small: |Ck| <= r - 1. Then there exist k1,...,kN+1 in {1,...,r} such that 0 is in conv{Pk1,1,...,PkN+1,N+1} and for any two distinct a,b in the same color class Ck we have ka != kb.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $r \ge 2$ and $N \ge 1$ be integers, with $N$ allowed to be taken sufficiently large compared to $r$. Suppose that $r(N+1)$ points $P_{i,j} \in \mathbb{R}^N$ are given, indexed by $1 \le i \le r$ and $1 \le j \le N+1$, and that for every $j \in \{1,\dots,N+1\}$ the origin satisfies
$$0 \in \operatorname{conv}\{P_{1,j}, P_{2,j}, \dots, P_{r,j}\}.$$
Suppose further that the index set $\{1,2,\dots,N+1\}$ is partitioned into color classes $C_1, C_2, \dots, C_m$, each of size at most $r-1$, i.e. $|C_k| \le r-1$ for all $k$.

Prove or disprove: there always exist indices $k_1, k_2, \dots, k_{N+1} \in \{1,\dots,r\}$ such that
$$0 \in \operatorname{conv}\{P_{k_1,1}, P_{k_2,2}, \dots, P_{k_{N+1},N+1}\},$$
and such that whenever $a, b$ are distinct elements of the same color class $C_k$, the chosen labels are distinct: $k_a \ne k_b$.
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published proof or refutation of this specific "multicolored Carathéodory" conjecture with small color classes. Related work concerns the classical colorful Carathéodory theorem and its computational/approximation versions, but no source confirms resolution of this exact statement. Status appears unknown / open.

status_evidence.title: Computational Aspects of the Colorful Carathéodory Theorem
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses k-colorful choices and colorful Carathéodory variants but does not resolve the multicolored conjecture with small color classes.
status_evidence.claim: Related colorful Carathéodory variants are studied, but the stated multicolored conjecture is not resolved here.

status_evidence.title: Colorful Caratheodory Revisited — Combinatorics and more
status_evidence.snippet: Survey-style discussion of colorful Carathéodory variants and conjectures, with no resolution of the small-color-class multicolored version.
status_evidence.claim: No resolution of the multicolored conjecture is reported.
